pack.name: Mastery · C2 Slang, Casual & Modern Work
pack.description: 15 natural C2 slang, casual everyday, and modern office expressions—real spoken English without textbook stiffness.

items.flat: I am quietly a bit relieved that they postponed the meeting until Monday.
items.upgraded: I'm low-key relieved they pushed the review to Monday—my Friday was already packed.

lines.speaker: Kasia
lines.text: Did you end up going to that huge rooftop party?

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: Nah, we kept it low-key and grabbed ramen around the corner instead.

lines.speaker: Marek
lines.text: Wait, did you actually like the soundtrack to that weird indie film?

lines.speaker: Chloe
lines.text: Okay, I'm low-key obsessed with it—I've had it on repeat all week.

items.nuance: Works two ways in modern English: as an adjective meaning understated/chill ('a low-key dinner') and as modern spoken slang adverb meaning 'quietly / slightly / secretly' ('I'm low-key nervous'). Avoid in formal emails, but super natural with friends and close teammates.
items.polish: po cichu / tak trochę (bez robienia hałasu) / na spokojnie
items.clozeSentence: That tiny noodle spot by the station is ___-key the best lunch in town.
items.clozeHint: 3-letter first half of the hyphenated slang modifier.
items.quizPrompt: Honestly, I secretly really liked their minimalist redesign even though everyone complained.
quizOptions: Honestly, I low-key loved the minimalist redesign.
Honestly, I under-key loved the minimalist redesign.
In a clandestine manner, I appreciated the minimalist redesign.
Honestly, I down-key loved the minimalist redesign.
quizExplanations: Completely natural modern spoken English with effortless tone.
Comically stiff for a casual opinion.
items.sandboxPrompt: Admit to a friend that you secretly enjoyed something slightly unexpected or want a quiet evening.
items.sandboxSample: I'm low-key glad it's pouring outside—gives me a guilt-free excuse to stay in and cook.
sandboxRubric: Register: Light, self-aware casual or slang tone.
Collocation: Used naturally before a verb/adjective ('low-key obsessed') or as an adjective ('a low-key night').
Cadence: Effortless and understated—never forced.

items.flat: Drinking hot coffee outside in crisp mountain air feels uniquely better than normal.
items.upgraded: Filter coffee at 6 a.m. after a cold mountain hike just hits different.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Have you listened to their live acoustic session yet?

lines.speaker: Ola
lines.text: Yeah, the second track hits different live—way more raw than the album cut.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Was it worth waking up at five to see the square empty?

lines.speaker: Zosia
lines.text: 100%—Rome with zero crowds hits different.

items.nuance: Modern everyday slang for an experience that lands with unusual emotional punch or satisfaction in a specific context. Notice it deliberately uses the bare form 'different' (not 'differently') as part of the fixed slang pattern.
items.polish: wchodzi zupełnie inaczej / ma całkiem inny klimat / smakuje o niebo lepiej
items.clozeSentence: Reading a real paperback on a long train ride just ___ different than scrolling on a phone.
items.clozeHint: 4-letter present verb meaning strikes or lands.
items.quizPrompt: Getting a sincere compliment from a tough mentor feels much more meaningful than usual.
quizOptions: Getting praise from a notoriously tough mentor just hits different.
Praise from a tough mentor strikes differently in feeling.
Getting praise from a tough mentor kicks different.
Praise from a strict mentor hits another way.
quizExplanations: Spot-on modern colloquial slang with natural rhythm.
Loses the idiomatic punch by turning it literal.
items.sandboxPrompt: Describe a simple everyday pleasure that feels uniquely better in a specific setting using 'hits different'.
items.sandboxSample: A Friday afternoon walk right after closing your laptop for a two-week vacation hits different.
sandboxRubric: Register: Warm, conversational modern slang.
Collocation: Exact fixed form '[subject] (just) hits different'.
Cadence: Sets up the vivid context before the punchline.

items.flat: He failed to notice the tense mood of the group and kept joking at the wrong time.
items.upgraded: He started pitching his side hustle right after the layoff news—seriously, read the room.

lines.speaker: Hannah
lines.text: Why did you cut the demo short?

lines.speaker: Piotr
lines.text: Tried to read the room—half the execs were already checking their watches.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Did Tom really complain about his bonus in front of the interns?

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: Zero ability to read the room, honestly.

items.nuance: Means picking up on unspoken social or emotional atmosphere. Used both positively ('she's great at reading the room') and as a sharp colloquial callout ('read the room!'). Works seamlessly in both casual chats and candid workplace debriefs.
items.polish: wyczuć klimat / zorientować się w nastrojach (na sali)
items.clozeSentence: Everyone was exhausted after a ten-hour flight, yet he didn't ___ the room and insisted on bar-hopping.
items.clozeHint: 4-letter verb meaning to interpret or sense.
items.quizPrompt: She immediately sensed that the team was stressed and kept her update brief.
quizOptions: She read the room right away and kept her update to two minutes.
She scanned the atmosphere of the chamber and spoke briefly.
She read the hall immediately and shortened her talk.
She felt the room immediately and stayed brief.
quizExplanations: Calqued from Polish 'wyczuć klimat'—English uses 'read the room'.
items.sandboxPrompt: Describe a moment in a meeting or dinner where someone either nailed or completely failed to sense the mood.
items.sandboxSample: I could tell nobody wanted a 40-slide deck at 5 p.m., so I read the room and jumped straight to the decision.
sandboxRubric: Register: Candid, socially perceptive.
Collocation: Exact idiom 'read the room'.
Cadence: Shows the social cue and the reaction clearly.

items.flat: You shouldn't underestimate or overlook that smaller neighborhood bakery—it's fantastic.
items.upgraded: Don't sleep on the small Vietnamese place by the tram stop—their pho beats everywhere downtown.

lines.speaker: Chris
lines.text: We've got two extra days in Poland after Kraków—any ideas?

lines.speaker: Ewa
lines.text: Don't sleep on Wrocław; the river islands and food scene are unreal.

lines.speaker: Devon
lines.text: Is browser IndexedDB worth learning over localStorage?

lines.speaker: Tomek
lines.text: Seriously, don't sleep on IndexedDB—it handles gigabytes offline without freezing the UI.

items.nuance: Vibrant modern slang meaning 'don't overlook / don't underestimate something underrated'. Note the crucial contrast with 'sleep on it' (which means 'wait until tomorrow to decide'). 'Don't sleep on X' (with a concrete noun/recommendation) means 'pay attention to X—it's great!'.
items.polish: nie lekceważ / nie przegap (bo to ukryta perełka)
items.clozeSentence: Everyone talks about Lisbon, but don't ___ on Porto—the coastal walks are incredible.
items.clozeHint: 5-letter verb meaning to overlook in this slang phrase.
items.quizPrompt: People overlook the built-in browser speech API, even though it works surprisingly well.
quizOptions: People really sleep on the built-in Web Speech API—it's shockingly capable.
People really nap over the built-in Web Speech API.
People are sleeping beside the Web Speech API without noticing.
People underestimate and slumber on the Web Speech API.
quizExplanations: Broken slang verb ('sleep on', never 'nap over').
items.sandboxPrompt: Recommend an underrated city, tool, restaurant, or habit using 'Don't sleep on...'.
items.sandboxSample: Don't sleep on morning walks without headphones—ten minutes of quiet resets your whole focus.
sandboxRubric: Register: Enthusiastic, insider recommendation tone.
Collocation: 'don't sleep on [noun]' (distinct from 'sleep on it').
Cadence: Brief concrete reason why it's underrated.

items.flat: I will be unreachable for a few hours this afternoon, and also that remark was totally inappropriate.
items.upgraded: Heads-up: I'll be out of pocket between 2 and 4 for a dentist appointment, then back on Slack.

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.text: Can you take a quick look at the staging deploy around 3?

lines.speaker: Owen
lines.text: I'm out of pocket until 4:30, but happy to review right after.

lines.speaker: Luke
lines.text: Did he really ask her salary in the middle of dinner?

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.text: Yeah, that comment was completely out of pocket.

items.nuance: True C2 register mastery means knowing all THREE live meanings of 'out of pocket': (1) Standard/financial: paying with your own cash ('paid $200 out of pocket'); (2) US workplace slang: temporarily unreachable/away from desk ('I'll be out of pocket until 3'); (3) Modern casual slang: wildly inappropriate or crossing a line ('that joke was out of pocket'). Context makes the sense unmistakable.
items.polish: nieosiągalny (w pracy) / grubo przesadzić, nie na miejscu (slang) / z własnej kieszeni
items.clozeSentence: Quick heads-up—I'll be out of ___ on a flight this morning, so ping Alex for anything urgent.
items.quizPrompt: Let your US teammates know casually on Slack that you'll be unreachable during the afternoon.
quizOptions: FYI, I'll be out of pocket from 1 to 3 today, then back online.
FYI, I will be outside my pocket from 1 to 3 today.
Please be advised I shall remain incommunicado from 1 to 3.
FYI, I'm out of wallet between 1 and 3 today.
quizExplanations: Spot-on modern US workplace Slack phrasing.
Broken fixed phrase ('out of pocket', never 'outside my pocket').
Comically stiff for a casual Slack update.
items.sandboxPrompt: Write either a casual Slack note saying you'll be unreachable, OR a casual reaction calling a rude remark wildly out of line.
items.sandboxSample: I'll be out of pocket on the train to Gdańsk until noon, so feel free to merge once CI is green.
sandboxRubric: Register: Matches the chosen sense (US office Slack OR casual slang).
Collocation: Exact idiom 'out of pocket'.
Cadence: Clear context so the intended meaning is unambiguous.

items.flat: That decision is so obviously beneficial that it requires almost no debate.
items.upgraded: At zero hosting cost and instant offline speed, moving to sharded JSON packs was a no-brainer.

lines.speaker: Founder
lines.text: Worth spending a day adding automated syntax checks to CI?

lines.speaker: Lead
lines.text: Total no-brainer—it already caught two broken quotes before deploy.

lines.speaker: Gosia
lines.text: Same rent, twice the light, and five minutes from the park?

lines.speaker: Kamil
lines.text: Honestly, that's a no-brainer—sign it before someone else does.

items.nuance: Punchy, informal-to-workplace slang for an obvious, low-effort win. Great in casual meetings, Slack, and conversations—just keep it out of ultra-formal board memos where 'straightforward call' or 'clear win' fits better.
items.polish: oczywista decyzja / nie ma się nad czym zastanawiać / pewniak
items.clozeSentence: With a 30-day free trial and zero lock-in, testing the new tool is a complete ___-brainer.
items.quizPrompt: Accepting a 20% raise with shorter commute is an obviously easy choice.
quizOptions: Higher pay and half the commute? That's a total no-brainer.
Higher pay and half the commute? That's a brainless choice.
That decision necessitates negligible cognitive deliberation.
Higher pay and half the commute? That's a zero-brain.
quizExplanations: 'Brainless' means stupid/foolish—the exact opposite of 'a no-brainer'!
items.sandboxPrompt: Describe a purchase, tool switch, or life decision that was an obvious win using 'a no-brainer'.
items.sandboxSample: Buying noise-canceling headphones before a twelve-hour flight was the easiest no-brainer of my year.
sandboxRubric: Register: Decisive, natural colloquial/workplace tone.
Collocation: Exact noun 'a (total/complete) no-brainer' (never 'brainless').
Cadence: Clearly shows why the upside is obvious.

items.flat: I completely support that idea and think we should definitely do it.
items.upgraded: If moving stand-up to async Slack saves everyone two hours a week, I'm all for it.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: Should we skip the fancy tasting menu and just split tapas?

lines.speaker: Dan
lines.text: I'm all for it—way more relaxed.

lines.speaker: Rachel
lines.text: Thinking of making Fridays no-meeting days across engineering.

lines.speaker: Bartek
lines.text: I'm all for trying that for a month and seeing how velocity looks.

items.nuance: Warm, enthusiastic endorsement that sounds far more human than 'I strongly agree with your proposal'. Works with 'it' ('I'm all for it') or a gerund/noun ('I'm all for keeping things simple').
items.polish: jestem jak najbardziej za / popieram w stu procentach
items.clozeSentence: If we can simplify the signup flow down to one screen, I'm ___ for it.
items.quizPrompt: I enthusiastically support taking the scenic train instead of flying.
quizOptions: Taking the night train instead of dealing with airport security? I'm all for it.
I am totally after taking the scenic train instead of flying.
I am all behind it to take the scenic train.
I am whole for taking the train.
quizExplanations: Slightly muddled idiom ('I'm all for it' or 'I'm 100% behind it', not 'all behind it to...').
items.sandboxPrompt: Enthusiastically back a friend's or teammate's practical suggestion using 'I'm all for...'.
items.sandboxSample: I'm all for keeping the interface calm and uncluttered—less chrome makes reading way easier.
sandboxRubric: Register: Warm, supportive, natural.
Collocation: 'be all for [it / noun / gerund]'.
Cadence: Concise enthusiasm with an optional brief reason.

items.flat: I forgot to send you the link yesterday because I was busy.
items.upgraded: Ah, sorry—sending the notes completely slipped my mind after the call. Dropping them here now.

lines.speaker: Julia
lines.text: Hey, did you grab the spare charger before leaving?

lines.speaker: Tomasz
lines.text: Ugh, it totally slipped my mind—I'll pick one up on the way.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Did you have a chance to ping finance about the invoice?

lines.speaker: Maja
lines.text: Honestly, it slipped my mind this morning—firing off the email right now.

items.nuance: Lighter and more graceful than the blunt 'I forgot'—implies an honest momentary lapse rather than carelessness. Pairing it immediately with the fix ('Dropping them here now') keeps accountability sharp.
items.clozeSentence: I meant to bring your book back today, and it completely ___ my mind.
items.clozeHint: Past tense verb meaning slid away unnoticed.
items.quizPrompt: I'm sorry, I totally forgot to attach the receipt to my expense report.
quizOptions: Sorry about that—attaching the receipt completely slipped my mind.
Sorry, the receipt totally fell out of my head.
Regrettably, the receipt escaped my cognitive retention.
Sorry, it slipped from my brain completely.
quizExplanations: Literal Polish calque ('wypadło mi z głowy').
Comically formal for an everyday slip-up.
Wrong noun and preposition ('slipped my mind', no 'from' and not 'brain').
items.sandboxPrompt: Politely own up to forgetting a small errand or link and follow immediately with the fix.
items.sandboxSample: Total honesty—forwarding the deck slipped my mind after lunch, so I'm sending it over right now.
sandboxRubric: Register: Candid, polite, zero melodrama.
Collocation: Exact idiom '[something] slipped my mind' (transitive, no 'from').
Cadence: Acknowledges the miss and resolves it immediately.

items.flat: Let's not make a strict plan now and just decide what to do depending on how things go.
items.upgraded: Weather looks unpredictable on Saturday, so let's play it by ear and decide over coffee.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Should we pre-book every museum for our three days in Vienna?

lines.speaker: Ola
lines.text: Let's book the Albertina and play the rest by ear.

lines.speaker: Lead
lines.text: How deep should we go into the technical architecture on slide four?

lines.speaker: Eng
lines.text: Let's play it by ear—if their CTO leans in, we'll unpack it; if not, we'll keep moving.

items.nuance: Musical metaphor (playing a tune without sheet music). Signals relaxed adaptability rather than poor planning. You can also swap 'it' for a noun ('play the afternoon by ear', 'play the rest by ear').
items.polish: zobaczymy na bieżąco / będziemy improwizować (w zależności od sytuacji)
items.clozeSentence: I'm not sure when my train gets in, so let's play dinner by ___.
items.clozeHint: 3-letter noun from playing music without a score.
items.quizPrompt: Let's stay flexible and decide how to spend Sunday morning once we wake up.
quizOptions: Let's play Sunday morning by ear depending on how tired we are.
Let's play Sunday morning by nose depending on our energy.
Let us improvise the morning schedule on the current basis.
Let's play it on ear once we wake up.
quizExplanations: Wrong body part ('by ear', never 'by nose').
Calque from Polish 'na bieżąco' + stiff wording.
items.sandboxPrompt: Suggest keeping weekend plans flexible because of weather or unpredictable timing.
items.sandboxSample: My flight lands right around rush hour, so let's play Friday evening by ear and text once I'm out of the airport.
sandboxRubric: Register: Easygoing, practical.
Collocation: 'play [it / noun] by ear'.
Cadence: Clearly explains why flexibility makes sense.

items.flat: We have worked enough for today, so let's stop now and pick this up tomorrow.
items.upgraded: All tests are green and the PR is up—let's call it a day and tackle polish with fresh eyes tomorrow.

lines.speaker: Kuba
lines.text: My brain is officially fried after debugging IndexedDB transactions.

lines.speaker: Sara
lines.text: Same—let's call it a day and grab a quick walk.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: One more drink or are we calling it a night?

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: Early flight tomorrow, so I'm calling it a night.

items.nuance: Clean, friendly way to wrap up work or an activity without sounding exhausted or abrupt. In the evening/social context, naturally shifts to 'call it a night'.
items.polish: fajrant / skończyć na dziś / zwinąć się na dzisiaj
items.clozeSentence: We've been staring at this spreadsheet since nine—let's ___ it a day.
items.quizPrompt: We've made solid progress; let's stop working for today and continue tomorrow morning.
quizOptions: Great progress today—let's call it a day and pick up fresh tomorrow.
Great progress today—let's name it a day and continue tomorrow.
Let us conclude our daily labors at this juncture.
Let's call it the day and finish tomorrow.
items.sandboxPrompt: Suggest wrapping up a long study or work session on a positive note using 'call it a day'.
items.sandboxSample: We just shipped the C2 pack and every check is green—let's call it a day while we're ahead.
sandboxRubric: Register: Relaxed, positive closure.
Collocation: Exact idiom 'call it a day' (or 'call it a night' in the evening).
Cadence: Smooth transition from accomplishment to stopping.

items.speechText: I wouldn't put it past him
items.flat: I would not be surprised at all if he actually stayed up all night rebuilding the app.
items.upgraded: Honestly, I wouldn't put it past him to rewrite the entire parser on a Sunday just for fun.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: Think Mark really brought his own hand-grinder on a camping trip?

lines.speaker: Ewa
lines.text: Oh, I wouldn't put it past him—the guy refuses to drink bad coffee.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Could the vendor try sneaking a renewal fee into the fine print?

lines.speaker: Zosia
lines.text: After last year? I wouldn't put it past them.

items.nuance: Wry, idiomatic C2 understatement meaning 'that sounds completely in character for them'—used either playfully for a friend's quirky dedication or skeptically for someone shady. Always takes 'to + verb' when naming the action ('wouldn't put it past her to...').
items.polish: wcale bym się po nim/niej tego nie zdziwił(a) / był(a)by do tego zdolny/a
items.clozeSentence: Wait, he biked forty kilometers in the rain for sourdough? Honestly, I wouldn't ___ it past him.
items.quizPrompt: Knowing her attention to detail, I wouldn't be surprised if she already built a spreadsheet for the trip.
quizOptions: I wouldn't put it past her to have color-coded the entire trip itinerary already.
I wouldn't place it behind her to organize the whole trip.
I would not deem it beyond her capacity to build a spreadsheet.
I wouldn't put it over her to make a spreadsheet.
quizExplanations: Wrong verb and preposition ('put it past', never 'place it behind').
items.sandboxPrompt: Playfully predict something totally in character for a friend or colleague using 'I wouldn't put it past...'.
items.sandboxSample: I wouldn't put it past her to show up to a casual hike with a full pour-over coffee kit in her backpack.
sandboxRubric: Register: Wry, playful, or shrewdly observant.
Collocation: 'wouldn't put it past [person] (to + verb)'.
Cadence: Specific detail makes the remark land.

items.flat: Can you give me a rough estimate of how long this task will take?
items.upgraded: No need for an exact quote yet—just give me a ballpark: are we talking days or weeks?

lines.speaker: PM
lines.text: Before we write a full RFC, can you give me a ballpark on the migration effort?

lines.speaker: Dev
lines.text: Rough ballpark, three to four days including tests.

lines.speaker: Buyer
lines.text: Are we even in the same ballpark on pricing?

lines.speaker: Rep
lines.text: Yeah, we're very close—just a few thousand apart annually.

items.nuance: Baseball metaphor meaning 'rough order-of-magnitude range'—takes the pressure off someone who hates committing to a premature exact number. Works as a noun ('a ballpark', 'in the right ballpark'), modifier ('ballpark figure'), or casual verb ('can you ballpark it?').
items.clozeSentence: Don't hold yourself to the hour—just give me a ___ figure so I can plan the sprint.
items.clozeHint: 8-letter compound noun from baseball meaning rough range.
items.quizPrompt: I don't need an exact budget yet, just a rough order-of-magnitude range.
quizOptions: No need for exact numbers yet—just give me a ballpark figure.
No need for exact numbers—just give me a stadium number.
Please supply a preliminary approximate magnitude range.
Just give me a playground figure for the budget.
quizExplanations: Way too stiff for a quick alignment check.
items.sandboxPrompt: Ask a teammate for a rough time or cost estimate without putting them on the spot.
items.sandboxSample: I know requirements are still shifting—just ballpark it for me: closer to $5k or $20k?
sandboxRubric: Register: Practical, low-pressure workplace tone.
Collocation: 'give a ballpark (figure)', 'in the same ballpark', or verb 'ballpark it'.
Cadence: Signals explicitly that rough precision is fine.

items.flat: I am currently too busy and mentally stretched to take on another project right now.
items.upgraded: I'd love to help with the workshop, but I genuinely don't have the bandwidth until next quarter.

lines.speaker: Manager
lines.text: Could you also mentor the new intern this month?

lines.speaker: Engineer
lines.text: I want to do it properly, and honestly I don't have the bandwidth while shipping v2.

lines.speaker: Nora
lines.text: Want to help organize the neighborhood swap meet next week?

lines.speaker: Kamil
lines.text: Love the idea, zero emotional bandwidth right now with the move.

items.nuance: Tech metaphor that crossed into everyday spoken English for both calendar time and mental/emotional capacity. Keeps a 'no' objective and boundary-clear rather than apologetic. Note: use naturally in moderation so it doesn't feel buzzwordy.
items.polish: nie mieć mocy przerobowych / nie mieć zasobów (czasu ani głowy)
items.clozeSentence: Between the audit and onboarding two new hires, the team simply doesn't have the ___ for a redesign.
items.clozeHint: 9-letter tech noun repurposed for personal/team capacity.
items.quizPrompt: Politely tell a colleague you don't have the time or mental space to take on an extra review this week.
quizOptions: I'd love to dig in, but I really don't have the bandwidth until Monday.
I don't have the frequency to review this document this week.
My processing capacity is currently depleted for additional tasks.
I am lacking the wifi to help with that this week.
items.sandboxPrompt: Decline an optional request politely by explaining your capacity and offering a realistic later window.
items.sandboxSample: I don't have the bandwidth to give this the review it deserves today, but I can block an hour Thursday morning.
sandboxRubric: Register: Calm, boundaried, modern workplace/casual tone.
Collocation: '(don't) have the bandwidth (for/to ...)' or 'zero bandwidth'.
Cadence: Pairs the honest 'no' with a clear timeline or alternative.

items.flat: Let's do a quick, rough calculation before building a detailed financial model.
items.upgraded: A quick back-of-the-envelope calculation shows 50,000 cards will take under 15 MB gzipped.

lines.speaker: Tech Lead
lines.text: Will IndexedDB run into quota limits if we load all of Wiktionary?

lines.speaker: Eng
lines.text: Back-of-the-envelope math: 20,000 rich cards is ~40 MB, well under browser limits.

lines.speaker: Founder
lines.text: Did finance finish the full forecast?

lines.speaker: COO
lines.text: Not yet, just a back-of-the-envelope estimate to sanity-check runway.

items.nuance: Describes a fast, pragmatic sanity-check calculation (as if jotted down on the back of a scrap envelope) before investing hours in a spreadsheet. Signals sharp engineering and business judgment.
items.polish: zgrubne wyliczenie „na kolanie” / szybka kalkulacja na serwetce
items.clozeSentence: Even on a back-of-the-___ estimate, automating the pipeline pays for itself in two weeks.
items.clozeHint: 8-letter noun for a paper letter cover.
items.quizPrompt: A quick rough sanity check shows the cloud bill won't exceed $50 a month.
quizOptions: Even a back-of-the-envelope calculation puts the monthly cloud bill under $50.
A calculation on the knee puts the cloud bill under $50.
A back-of-the-letter calculation puts the bill under $50.
An elementary preliminary arithmetic estimate shows $50.
quizExplanations: Sharp, idiomatic, and standard in tech/finance.
items.sandboxPrompt: Share a quick sanity-check calculation for a project, trip, or storage estimate using 'back-of-the-envelope'.
items.sandboxSample: Doing quick back-of-the-envelope math, studying seven new cards a day adds up to over 2,500 phrases a year.
sandboxRubric: Register: Crisp, pragmatic, analytical.
Collocation: 'back-of-the-envelope math / calculation / estimate'.
Cadence: Connects the quick rough math directly to a useful takeaway.

items.flat: They shouldn't just approve the proposal automatically without actually reviewing the details.
items.upgraded: Security review isn't a rubber-stamp step—build at least three days into the schedule for real feedback.

lines.speaker: Reviewer
lines.text: Why did that regression slip through review?

lines.speaker: Lead
lines.text: Because the PR was 2,000 lines and got rubber-stamped five minutes before release.

lines.speaker: Director
lines.text: Think the committee will push back on the Q4 budget?

lines.speaker: CFO
lines.text: Definitely—they're not going to rubber-stamp headcount this year.

items.nuance: Vivid verb and modifier for mindless, automatic approval without real scrutiny. Almost always carries a critical or cautionary edge—great for calling out weak review processes without attacking individuals.
items.polish: przyklepać (bez czytania / z automatu) / czysta formalność
items.clozeSentence: Don't expect legal to ___-stamp a brand-new enterprise contract overnight.
items.quizPrompt: The review process shouldn't be an automatic approval with zero real inspection.
quizOptions: PR review shouldn't be a rubber-stamp exercise—we want genuine scrutiny.
PR review shouldn't be a plastic-stamp process with no reading.
PR review should avoid perfunctory automatic endorsement.
PR review shouldn't just glue-stamp every branch.
quizExplanations: Accurate meaning, but stiff and overly academic.
items.sandboxPrompt: Warn a team not to treat a review or sign-off step as a mere formality using 'rubber-stamp'.
items.sandboxSample: If we rush the design sign-off on Friday afternoon, people will just rubber-stamp it and catch issues during QA.
sandboxRubric: Register: Candid, quality-focused workplace tone.
Collocation: Verb 'rubber-stamp [something]' or modifier 'a rubber-stamp [step/process]'.
Cadence: Clearly contrasts mindless approval with real review.
